messages.author: fb5d69b072117c9e
messages.subject: ddply and POSIXct variables
parts:
Hi All,

I've been beating my head on this for several days and can't seem to
find a solution. Plyr is not subsetting my data.frame correctly when I
subset on more than one POSIXct variable. Unfortunately I can't share
the data and I haven't been able to create a test case but hopefully
the info below will be enough for someone to suggest a solution.

> str(df)
'data.frame': 309767 obs. of 4 variables:
$ A_ID : chr "ABR20X7G1135" "FMJA8971A203" "FMJA7552A190"
"FMJA7552A190" ...
$ B_ID : chr "AVR20X8G1135" "FMJA8971A203" "FMJA7552A190"
"FMJA7552A190" ...
$ departure.time: POSIXct, format: "2010-05-15 07:13:00" "2010-07-22
10:50:00" "2010-07-09 14:44:00" "2010-07-09 14:44:00" ...
$ arrival.time : POSIXct, format: "2010-05-15 12:46:00" "2010-07-22
11:45:00" "2010-07-09 15:44:00" "2010-07-09 15:44:00" ...

Here's the first problem - should this return the same result?

> nrow(unique(df))
[1] 44915
> ids <- id(df, drop = TRUE)
max(ids)
[1] 43528

Because it does when I drop one of the POSIXct variables

> nrow(unique(df[,1:3]))
[1] 41934
> ids <- id(df[,1:3], drop = TRUE)
max(ids)
[1] 41934

In short, help! What am I doing wrong here?

-ricardo

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: ddply and POSIXct variables
parts:
Hi Ricardo,

It's pretty much impossible for me to offer any suggestions without a
reproducible example, so all I can suggest is that you spend a bit
more time trying to isolate the specific feature of your data that is
causing the problem. It's certainly suggestive that ids is returning
the incorrect result.

Hadley
